decisions.reason: Product A is a core bread closely tied to existing recipes and production knowledge, so the firm can readily learn from it and is unlikely to drop it.

Guided historic mill tour builds on the firm’s hospitality and tour operations but is less tied to core baking knowledge, so absorptive capacity is moderate and the risk of dropping is higher though still manageable.
Sweet pastry fits the firm’s traditional confectionery skills and existing customer base, enabling effective learning and improvement with low drop risk.
Crusty farmhouse bread is close to the firm’s established bread portfolio, so it can leverage existing baking knowledge and is likely to be retained.
Poppy seed Christmas stollen is a flagship seasonal product close to existing recipes and has received a gold award, so the firm has strong absorptive capacity and high commitment to keeping it.
Premium Christmas stollen is close to established stollen recipes and has been recognized with a gold award, making it a low-risk, high-fit product the firm will keep.
